title: Yttrium Superhydrides Revisited: Advanced Experimental and Theoretical Studies of YH$_6$, YH$_9$ and YH$_{10}$
authors: Dmitrii V. Semenok, Pedro N. Ferreira, Di Zhou, Fabian Jőbstl, Andrey V. Sadakov, Kirill S. Pervakov, Burkhan I. Massalimov, Toni Helm, Ryosuke Akashi, Vladimir M. Pudalov, Viktor V. Struzhkin, Christoph Heil, Ivan A. Troyan
abstract: Yttrium polyhydrides are benchmark materials in high-pressure superconductivity, yet several key properties of the Y-H system remain insufficiently characterized. Here we combine contact transport, contactless radio-frequency measurements, pulsed-field experiments, and first-principles calculations to reinvestigate YH$_6$, YH$_9$, and YH$_{10}$ in the pressure range 140-213 GPa. Yttrium hydrides YH$_6$ ($\textit{$T_c$}$ = 218-221 K) and YH$_9$ ($\textit{$T_c$}$ = 235-237 K) demonstrate narrow superconducting transitions ($\textit{$Δ$T$_c$}$ = 2-5 K), approaching the limit imposed by thermal fluctuations. Pulsed-field measurements on YH$_6$ up to 60 T establish an extended superconducting phase diagram with a linear slope $\textit{dB$_{c2}$/dT}$ = -0.52 T/K, pronounced transition broadening above 30 T, and negligible normal-state magnetoresistance. We report the radio-frequency AC susceptibility study of YH$_6$, providing evidence for superconductivity via high-frequency field screening in a contactless geometry. Experiments involving Pd incorporation, Pd thin-film sputtering, and Al alloying show strong suppression of high-temperature superconductivity, with no transitions detected above 78-120 K. Finally, using density-functional theory with the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation, superconducting density-functional theory, and full-bandwidth Migdal-Eliashberg calculations, we show that anharmonic effects substantially reduce the predicted $\textit{$T_c$}$ of cubic YH$_{10}$ to approximately 260-270 K. These results strongly disfavor room-temperature superconductivity in binary yttrium superhydrides.
summary: This work comprehensively re-examines yttrium superhydrides using multiple experimental techniques and advanced theoretical calculations. The findings consistently point to limitations in the superconducting state of these binary compounds, particularly arguing against room-temperature superconductivity based on measured critical fields and calculated $T_c$ reductions.
main_problem: To re-investigate the superconducting potential of yttrium polyhydrides ($	ext{YH}_6$, $	ext{YH}_9$, and $	ext{YH}_{10}$) under high pressure, specifically addressing claims of room-temperature superconductivity.
main_result: The combination of advanced measurements (pulsed fields, RF susceptibility) and theoretical calculations strongly disfavors the existence of room-temperature superconductivity in binary yttrium superhydrides.
method: A combined approach using experimental techniques like pulsed-field magnetometry, contactless radio-frequency AC susceptibility, and electrical transport measurements, alongside sophisticated first-principles calculations (DFT, Migdal-Eliashberg theory).
model_or_system: The study focuses on the superconducting properties of yttrium hydrides ($	ext{YH}_x$) synthesized and tested within Diamond Anvil Cells under pressures up to 213 GPa.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), upper critical magnetic field ($	ext{B}_{c2}(T)$), AC magnetic susceptibility (field screening), and normal-state magnetoresistance.
important_parameters: Pressure range of 140–213 GPa; superconducting transitions observed at $T_c \approx 218-237$ K for $	ext{YH}_6$ and $	ext{YH}_9$.
main_assumptions: The theoretical modeling incorporates anharmonic effects, which are crucial in reducing the predicted $T_c$ of $	ext{YH}_{10}$ to a more realistic range.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows electric transport measurements ($R(T)$ vs. T and B) for $	ext{YH}_6$; Figure 2 details RF transmission measurements confirming superconductivity in $	ext{YH}_6$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically combines experimental characterization (transport, RF, pulsed fields) to map out the superconducting phase diagram of $	ext{YH}_x$, followed by theoretical calculations that refine and constrain the predicted critical temperatures.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity rather than quantum information, the rigorous application of advanced many-body theory (Migdal-Eliashberg) combined with high-pressure experimental diagnostics provides a model for testing fundamental condensed matter theories under extreme conditions.
